rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3 - the authors run the ISAREG soil water balance model, calibrated and validated with their own 2001-2003 field experiments at the Azizbek-1 farm (Fig. 1 compares observed and simulated soil water content and reports good agreement). Q2: Sections 2.1, 3.2-3.3, Tables 7-13 - the model, using the Stewart/Doorenbos-Kassam water-yield response function (Eq. 2, Ky=1.11) and FAO56 ET methodology, is used to search full and deficit irrigation schedules to cope with water scarcity, reporting water savings, RYL, WP and EWP for 2001-2003 and for average/high/very high demand years; simulated soil water was checked against observations (Fig. 1) and simulated yields are said to be in accordance with field experiments. Q4: Tables 6-8, 10-12, Figs. 4-6 - the model computes the intermediate variables (available soil water, deep percolation, groundwater contribution, ETa/ETc deficit) through which the schedules reduce water use and affect yield. Q7: Section 3.2.3 and Conclusions - the authors state from their results that water-saving strategies require improved farm irrigation systems able to apply the preferred depths, delayed first irrigation to favour root development, and improved delivery scheduling and furrow irrigation performance. Q8: Section 3.1 and Conclusions - authors note that the years with daily data (2001-2003) are of low climatic demand, 2003 being the most humid year of the series, so that analysis refers to a wet period; Section 3.2.3 notes simulated WP is slightly higher than field values because larger depths were applied in the field.
rows.notes: Single site (one experimental farm, loam/clay-loam soils), single crop (cotton), one method (calibrated simulation model); years and demand scenarios are not sites. No standard deviations, confidence intervals or propagated uncertainty are reported for the scheduling results; the frequency analysis of NIR over 1970-2003 (Fig. 2) selects scenario years rather than quantifying dispersion of the claimed result, so Q9 is answered no. The passage also mentions salinity, which is addressed in Pereira et al. (2007), not in this paper; this study covers the water-scarcity part of the claim.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a model-based irrigation scheduling analysis (ISAREG with FAO56 Kc-ETo and Doorenbos-Kassam water-yield function) calibrated and validated with field soil-water data from Fergana; it is itself the example the passage refers to.
